study: Dolfin et al. 2019 (Teacher Potential Project [TPP]; EL Education ELA curriculum + embedded PD/coaching)
eval_evidence: Independent evaluation by Mathematica (submitted to EL Education); conducted under an i3 validation grant to EL Education but the impact study was carried out by Mathematica, a third-party evaluator.
developer_evidence: EL Education (the developer) designed and delivered TPP: on-site institutes plus 'on-site and video-based coaching from EL Education coaches, including observations, modeling, lesson studies.'
cascade_evidence: EL Education coaches worked directly with the participating ELA teachers (institutes + classroom coaching); no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools continued their business-as-usual district ELA curriculum and professional development; design note describes BAU comparison.
coaching_evidence: Intensive in-class coaching: ~21 days of on-site plus 3 days of video-based coaching per school in Year 1 (fewer in Year 2), with monthly lesson-study sessions; teachers were expected to participate in coaching at least 10 times during the school year.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention is a teacher-facing ELA curriculum plus embedded PD/coaching delivered through the teacher's regular ELA instruction; no tutoring, pull-out, or extra student dose.
maturity_evidence: Reported headline/confirmatory impacts are the two-year impacts (S4 overall and S6 two-year schools), measured after a prior implementation year. A clean one-year (first-year) full-sample contrast (S2) is also reported and was null; impacts emerged only after two years.
